title: Fix Critical Production Readiness Issues
decision: Execute a 3-phase stabilization effort targeting all CRITICAL issues identified in code review (2026-08-20). Phase 1 fixes Security & Stability (secrets redaction, error isolation, db crash fix). Phase 2 fixes Data Integrity (persistent event store, history archive persistence, DLQ drain, optimistic concurrency). Phase 3 enforces Architecture Compliance (context budget enforcement, test runner timeout, idempotency fix, event type dedup). No new features accepted during SPRINT-NF-CR-001.
rationale: 14 CRITICAL issues block production deployment: secrets sent to LLM without redaction (arch ch.46), events lost on restart (ch.43), dead-letter queue grows unbounded, subscription handler crashes kill entire event pipeline, concurrent workflow transitions overwrite state silently. Context budget is advisory-only (ch.49), test runner has no timeout (ch.44), history archive is in-memory-only (ch.34). Overall architecture compliance is ~73% — functional but not safe for production. Fixing these issues brings compliance above 95%.
alternatives: Defer all fixes — ship current code and patch critical bugs reactively. Risk: data loss, secret leaks, crashes under load.
Fix everything in one sprint — too many changes, high merge conflict risk, hard to verify individually.
Phase by module instead of severity — slower security exposure window, harder to measure progress.
consequences: Positive: Secrets protection eliminates credential leak risk. Persistent stores survive Node restarts. Error isolation prevents single-handler crashes cascading system-wide.
Negative: Adds ~15-20 engineering days of work. Introduces migration complexity for event store and history tables.
Trade-off: New sprint blocks feature development temporarily. All team capacity directed at stability.
Long-term: Foundation enables future work (multi-project, advanced memory, dashboard UI) with confidence in data integrity.
